messages: oliver: Quick design check — I'm iterating on the autoscale empty state when users have min==max or burst disabled. Current problem: CTA copy and affordance are confusing. maria: yep saw the mock, main thing for me is clarity: users need to know whether min==max means autoscale is off or it's just a fixed floor. aj: +1. Product asks: is this the same UI we show for dedicated pools and hosted pools? we need consistent wording. oliver: Right now mocks show header: `Fixed capacity` and a subtle line: "Autoscale off — min and max are equal". But the CTA says `Enable burst` which is misleading when burst isn't available for that pool. priya: technical constraint: some GPU pools don't support burst (preemptible/no-burst). We should surface availability earlier — maybe disable the CTA and add tooltip. maria: proposal: header becomes `Capacity locked` (strong), subcopy: `Min and max are equal — this pool won't scale above X GPUs.` CTA: `Allow autoscale` (primary) or `Edit capacity` (secondary). Disabled CTA state when burst not supported: tooltip: `Burst not supported on this pool`. sam: concerned about discoverability — if we swap CTA to `Allow autoscale`, does that trigger a bulk change? We need confirm modal. Also keyboard users should be able to tab to the tooltip. oliver: good call. For keyboard/ARIA: tooltip must be focusable and the CTA should have `aria-disabled` with an explanatory `aria-describedby` pointing to the message. Example snippet: ``` Burst not supported on this pool ``` maria: copy nit: avoid `Allow autoscale` — it sounds permissive. Maybe `Turn on autoscaling` or `Enable autoscaling` (clearer verb). aj: `Enable autoscaling` feels more actiony. Also we should surface estimated cost delta inline (small muted text) — eg `≈ +$0.15 / hour if autoscaled` so teams understand impact. priya: we can compute a ballpark cost from current pool profile; engineering can add that as an optional line. Need to confirm we have permission to show cost estimates for private deployments. sam: accessibility: color contrast on the `Fixed capacity` badge is borderline in dark mode. Also voiceover should read: `Capacity locked, min equals max, autoscaling disabled` — maybe concatenate a hidden string for screen readers. maria: microcopy suggestion for guardrail: when SLO slider is at extreme low latency and min==max, show inline warning: `Selected SLO may require reserving more GPUs. We suggest enabling autoscaling or raising the min.` small `Learn more` link to docs. oliver: love that. Final UI changes I'm proposing: - Header: `Capacity locked` - Subcopy: `Min and max are equal — this pool won't scale above {max} GPUs.` - Primary CTA: `Enable autoscaling` (disabled with tooltip if not supported) - Secondary: `Edit capacity` - Inline muted row: `Est. cost delta: {value}` when data available - Screen-reader only: `Autoscaling is currently disabled for this pool` aj: one more ask — when user toggles `Enable autoscaling`, open a tiny inline confirmation (not full modal) with `Are you sure? Autoscaling will allow pool size to change between {min} and {max2}.` Buttons: `Confirm` / `Cancel`. Keep it keyboard-friendly. priya: implementationally, the inline confirm can be a `role=dialog` that traps focus temporarily. We can re-use existing component from pool-switcher. design-bot: deploy-preview available at https://preview.redwood.design/branch/autoscale-emptystate — includes dark mode and keyboard walkthrough. maria: I'll iterate copy and push a new figma frame with the ARIA hints. tagging @aj for final product wording signoff. oliver: thanks everyone — I'll update the spec and add acceptance criteria for accessibility and cost line. Will follow up with a quick QA checklist.
